commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[grafana] Narrow Finelog training discovery queries (#9260)

Discover training dashboard runs from process-zero `phase` heartbeats
rather than every stepped metric row. The production 12-hour selector
returned the same 123 runs and fell from 2.93 seconds to 1.49 seconds.

Limit broad hero phase enrollment to the one-hour enrollment window. If
Iris still reports an active run after its phase heartbeat ages out,
recover that run's execution identity with an exact 24-hour cluster and
`run_id` query. The fallback preserves silent-run alert behavior while
allowing Finelog to use the existing `run_id` partitions.
`levanter.metrics` intentionally remains without secondary indexes.

The September 17 Grafana alert change routed transient failures through
alert endpoints but did not change these SQL probes. The September 2
change renamed one evaluation metric. The last query-shape change was
the August 26 partitioning rollout.

Incident: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/478

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Filter repeated tool calls after identical replies (#9259)

Filter chat records when the assistant repeats the same tool call a
third time after the first two calls return identical text. The sequence
must occur before the next user message, with each call following its
preceding reply. Parallel tool batches remain valid. The filter has its
own counter and does not count toward the 5% malformed-record health
limit.

A sample audit of 210,031 conversations across 246 SFT sources found 101
matching traces in 19 sources. The chat normalization version changes so
downstream artifacts will be rebuilt on the next run. Records ending in
a tool call remain valid because some environments use a terminal tool
to finish a task.

commits.message:
[grug] Reuse QB-routed MoE (#9238)

Add QBRoutedMoE to own common QB routing, padding-aware dispatch, and
routing metrics. Model wrappers retain router and expert parameter

while preserving its deferred scan collective, latent expert path, and

Require final answers or tool calls at chat turn boundaries (#9243)

Require normalized chat records to finish assistant turns with a final
answer or tool call. This prevents an end-of-turn token immediately
after reasoning or ordinary commentary. User followups after completed
tool observations remain valid.

Bump the normalization version so existing outputs are revalidated.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Let Harbor load Hugging Face task datasets (#9254)

Pass `hf://` dataset selectors to Harbor in both preflight and
evaluation workers. The pinned Harbor runtime downloads the snapshot and
loads its task directories, so Marin no longer makes a second copy or
substitutes a local path. Marin still rebases workspace-local datasets
and forwards `HF_TOKEN` for gated repositories.

This uses the merged Harbor loader from [Harbor
#160](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/160). A moving
`ref: main` can still change between preflight and execution.

The safe Marin suite passed with 1,957 tests, five skips, and five
expected failures. An isolated preflight with a fake one-task HF
snapshot returned `hf://example/tasks` as the benchmark task with count
one. The merged Harbor pin passed the external lock check and isolated
import.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Repair the eval launcher for chat-served and reasoning models (#9251)

Marin's Evalchemy client (marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py, the
script the eval job runs once per task to build and run the evalchemy
command) no longer loads the checkpoint tokenizer on chat routes. The
endpoint applies the chat template, and the client-side load rejected
Kimi-Linear (custom tokenizer code) and Gemma 4 (tokenizer metadata in
the Transformers 5 format, which Evalchemy's pinned Transformers 4.57
cannot parse). Loglikelihood tasks still load it with trust_remote_code.
The eval job also forwards JUDGE_API_KEY, JUDGE_BASE_URL and JUDGE_MODEL
so FinanceBench can reach its judge; #9070 tracks passing judge
credentials through a secret mechanism, and this forwarding is the
interim path.

The Harbor preflight materializes hf:// datasets. Since #9145 it passed
the raw hf:// name to Harbor's registry package validator, which
rejected every Hugging Face-backed policy at launch. The preflight now
downloads the snapshot into the Hugging Face cache with 32 workers (13 s
warm, 267 s cold for the SWE-bench folders) and hands Harbor a local
task tree, the same shape the worker builds at run time. HF_TOKEN
reaches the preflight for gated repositories.

Generation budgets come from the served context or the model config
instead of a per-config cap. Every generation config carried an explicit
max_tokens (128 for TriviaQA, 1024 for the code suites, 8192 for AIME24,
32768 for OlympiadBench) that the client sent as both --max_tokens and
gen_kwargs max_gen_toks. Reasoning models hit those caps inside their
chains: 64 of 180 Qwen3.6 OlympiadBench requests and 17,925 of 17,944
TriviaQA requests ended truncated with no final answer, and Qwen3.6
scored 0.023 on AIME24. max_tokens is now optional end to end and
removed from every generation config except MRCR, the long-context
retrieval benchmark whose prompts are built to fill an explicit
max_length. An Evalchemy chat benchmark then derives its budget from the
served context minus its stored longest prompt (evalchemy#132); AIME24
on a 73,664-token context gets 72,898 output tokens. An lm-eval-native
generation task only reads max_gen_toks and would fall back to lm-eval's
256-token default, so the client hands it the served context minus a
4,096-token prompt reserve. A model config's generation.max_gen_toks
overrides both paths. The client tells chat benchmarks from lm-eval
tasks by their directory under Evalchemy's eval/chat_benchmarks.

The Evalchemy pin advances 412ae9c2 -> 9447eed9: the code sandbox
preloads numpy before reliability_guard nulls os.putenv, which had
scored every HumanEvalPlus and MBPPPlus sample 0.0 since evalchemy#111
(evalchemy#137; Qwen3-Coder HumanEvalPlus reads 0.878 after); served
chat models initialize without a client tokenizer (#140); infrastructure
failures are recorded per sample and per task instead of failing the run
(#141, #142, #143, #144); when some FinanceBench judge requests fail,
the trials the judge did grade keep their labels and the failed ones are
recorded as grader infrastructure (#145); Gemma 4's list-valued
extra_special_tokens loads under Transformers 4.57 (#146); MBPPPlus and
HumanEvalPlus grade indented solutions that previously raised
IndentationError (#148). The Harbor pin advances ec23913e -> 16ba2893:
the terminus-2 agent accepts extra_body given as a JSON string
(harbor#158), and DS-1000 tasks grade the file the instruction tells the
agent to write, where every agentic trial had scored 0 before
(harbor#159).

Fixes #9227 (client tokenizer load on chat routes). Fixes #9229 (Harbor
preflight hf:// datasets). Part of #8083.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Register Open-SWE-Traces structured chat sources (#9245)

Register each release, agent harness, model, and task combination in the
pinned v1.0, v1.1, and v1.2
[Open-SWE-Traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Open-SWE-Traces)
data as a structured chat source, 13 in total. Preserve the recorded
issue prompts, reasoning, tool definitions, calls, observations, and
`resolved` task-success field in normalized chat. Render the
conversation with Marin's chat template.

The export omits tool-call IDs on observations. Assign each observation
to the next outstanding call, including when an assistant issues
parallel calls. The Hugging Face file list shows that all 212 Parquet
shards map to exactly one source. Thirty sampled trajectories across the
three releases converted, normalized, and rendered without rejection.
The full download and conversion pipeline has not run.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Register Nemotron v3 structured chat sources (#9237)

Register 75 structured chat partitions from 21 pinned datasets in
NVIDIA's Nemotron post-training v3 collection. Source roles, reasoning,
tool calls, and available tool schemas pass through Harmony
normalization. Anonymized names such as `NAME_1` remain in the source
text. The Instruction-Following-Chat-v3 chat split restores withheld
WildChat and LMSYS seed prompts by SHA-256 against pinned source
datasets before conversion.

Competitive-Programming-v1 remains excluded: a released Python row
(`e50e6e27ab80d625d56a2bc8fdadc7be`) has `messages[0].content == "-"`
and no recovery key. SWE-v3 remains excluded because its tool calls lack
source tool definitions. Empty conversations, interrupted tool exchanges
before a later turn, and pathological repeated lines are filtered.
Terminal unanswered tool calls are preserved. For SWE-v2 agentless, the
adapter removes an exact `<think>`/`<solution>` output-format suffix.
This retained 44 otherwise rejected issue examples in a 100-row sample.
Source `train_turns` annotations remain in the chat artifact, but the
current trainer applies loss to every assistant turn.

Full dataset materialization has not run. Restoring LMSYS prompts
requires access to its gated source dataset at execution time.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[inference] Add Chat tools and simulated agent workspaces (#9204)

Let users define typed Python functions and attach simulated agent
workspaces in the Iris Chat UI. The dashboard converts annotated
signatures and docstrings into OpenAI function schemas and exposes each
enabled workspace as a conventional `bash(command)` tool. Both use the
standard `tools` request field, so the active tokenizer template renders
their calls and results. Browser conversations persist Python source,
initial workspace files, and replayable command history. Empty chats
include two Python examples and three agent tasks for code repair, log
investigation, and configuration changes.

Tool exchange follows the served model's active, tool-aware tokenizer
template. The dashboard's `/info` response includes generated-output
conventions extracted from that template. Direct vLLM and Levanter
serving use the template loaded by their backend. Brokered serving uses
an explicitly configured template when present and otherwise loads the
configured tokenizer's tool-aware template. The browser recognizes the
call delimiters used by Marin's Datakit and Delphi templates, the bare
`name`/`parameters` JSON emitted by the repository's Llama 3 template,
and structured OpenAI `tool_calls` from servers that parse calls
themselves.

The More options panel exposes `enable_thinking` and
`custom_instructions` as `chat_template_kwargs`. A Raw chat toggle
replaces rendered messages with one role-labeled plain-text transcript
containing the system and user messages, unparsed assistant response
fields, structured tool calls, tool results, and errors. Normal parsing
and tool execution continue while this view is active. Reasoning parsing
uses the active template's delimiters and recognizes the repository's
known thinking-token pairs when metadata is absent or stale.

Assistant calls and tool results remain structured messages in
conversation history. Subsequent requests include assistant `tool_calls`
and matching `role: "tool"` messages, so the backend renders results
through the same model template. Validation and invocation failures
become matching tool results that the model can recover from. An
interrupted round receives cancellation results, and the UI stops after
eight consecutive tool rounds.

Python schema discovery parses function syntax without executing it.
Pydantic validates and coerces arguments before invocation and validates
return values afterward. Functions must be synchronous and use the
documented JSON-compatible annotation subset. Each invocation runs in a
fresh ShellSim environment without access to the host filesystem,
processes, network, environment variables, or clock. The simulation
allows 10 million CPU ticks, 64 MiB of memory, 4 MiB of disk, and 1 MiB
of output. An outer worker enforces a 10-second wall timeout, and
submitted source is limited to 64 KiB.

Agent workspaces reconstruct their initial files and replay prior
commands before each Bash call, preserving edits and simulated Git state
without retaining a host process or directory. Initial files receive a
fresh Git baseline. Users can seed files as JSON or load a public GitHub
repository's default-branch snapshot outside ShellSim; credentials,
remote history, submodules, binary files, and generated directories are
excluded. Imports are limited to 500 text files, 256 KiB per file, 4 MiB
total text, and a 4 MiB compressed archive. Workspace simulations allow
50 million CPU ticks, 64 MiB of memory, 16 MiB of disk, and 2 MiB of
output, with at most 32 replayed commands. ShellSim implements simulated
Bash and Python subsets, so unsupported commands and language features
return tool errors.

The Iris dashboard capability URL authorizes inference, simulated tools,
workspace commands, and bounded public GitHub downloads. Share it only
with trusted users and treat it as a credential.

Co-authored-by: William Held <9847335+Helw150@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Preserve Terminus protocol and filter AgentTrove sources (#9239)

Preserve the full initial Terminus prompt, including its JSON response
schema, and each assistant JSON object containing `commands`. Keep
terminal output as user turns. This fixes the rendered SFT examples for
AgentTrove, Nemotron Terminal, and Penfever's Terminus rollouts.
Terminal observations containing malformed tool wrappers remain
filtered.

Drop AgentTrove chat rows whose `original_source` is `freelancer`,
`Inferred Bugs`, `MagiCoder Evol Instruct`, `exp_rpt`, `exp_rle`, or
`unknown`. A [15-row sample of
`freelancer`](https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?dataset=open-thoughts%2FAgentTrove&config=default&split=train&offset=499995&length=15&revision=b395a43)
contains job postings, including open-ended app requests and a recruiter
role, with repeated task IDs. The [TaskTrove v5.1
audit](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/TaskTrove/blob/96567362fa3c41208e0954317c53767023b420eb/audits/v5.1/INDEPENDENT_ANALYSIS.md)
rejected the Inferred Bugs, Nemotron C++, and Magicoder task lineages;
its [release
history](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/TaskTrove/blob/96567362fa3c41208e0954317c53767023b420eb/README.md)
records other retired freelancer, `exp_rle`, `exp_rpt`, and `exp_flat25`
lineages. AgentTrove folds several upstream repositories into each of
`exp_rpt`, `exp_rle`, and `unknown`. Filtering those whole labels
intentionally discards some tasks that may be sound to avoid pulling in
deprecated envs.
